title: 1. Hook: The One-Man Army vs The Mega Corporation
text: Imagine a tiny roadside tea stall. The owner does everything: makes the tea, serves the customers, cleans the cups, and manages the money. Now imagine a massive company like Amazon or Tata. Can one person do everything there? No! They have different departments for shipping, software, HR, and sales. Similarly, an Amoeba is like that tea stall—one cell does everything. But your body is like a Mega Corporation. How does your body manage billions of cells?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking: The Division of Labour
text: If every cell in a human body tried to digest food, breathe, pump blood, and think all at the same time, it would be complete chaos! Why do you think our body groups certain cells together instead of letting every cell do its own thing?

content.title: 3. Discovery: The Cell Factory
content.description: Watch how similar cells group together to perform a specific function, just like workers forming a specialized team.

title: 4. Reveal: The Definition of Tissue
text: In multicellular organisms, cells that are similar in structure and work together to achieve a particular function form a **Tissue**. Blood, phloem, and muscle are all examples of tissues. The division of labour in multicellular organisms is achieved through these tissues.

content.description: A group of cells that are similar in structure and/or work together to achieve a particular function.

content.text: Think of the hierarchy: Cells -> Tissues -> Organs -> Organ Systems -> Organism.

content.question: Which of the following best describes a tissue?
options: A single cell performing all functions
A group of similar cells working together to perform a specific function
A complete organ like the heart

content.text: Mistaking an organ (like the heart) for a tissue. The heart is made of DIFFERENT tissues (muscle, nerve, blood) working together.

title: 6. Reflection: Plants vs Animals
text: Take a moment to think. Plants stand still in one place their entire lives. Animals move around looking for food, mates, and shelter. Do you think plants and animals need the exact same types of tissues?

title: 7. Connection: Linking back to Cells
text: Remember when we studied the 'Fundamental Unit of Life' (Cells)? You learned that plant cells have a rigid cell wall, while animal cells do not. Because their fundamental units are different, the tissues they form are also drastically different, perfectly suited to their different lifestyles.

content.title: 8. Mastery: The Tissue Detective
content.instructions: Go to your garden or look at a potted plant. Touch the bark of a tree, and then touch a soft, growing leaf. The bark is dead tissue, providing strength. The green leaf has living tissue, making food. Most of a plant's tissues are dead, to provide mechanical strength with less maintenance! For humans, almost all tissues are living.
